title: The Horse and the Ass

full_text:
A country peddler was traveling to the city market with his two beasts of burden: a proud, sleek warhorse adorned with brass-studded harness, and a patient, humble little donkey. The peddler had loaded all the heavy packs, iron pots, and sacks of grain onto the donkey's back, while the horse pranced alongside carrying nothing but his light leather saddle.

As the sun rose higher and the road climbed a steep, stony mountain pass, the little donkey's knees began to buckle beneath the crushing weight. Gasping for breath, he turned to the proud horse and pleaded:

"Good brother, I beg you, take a small portion of my burden! Even a single sack would relieve my distress and allow me to survive this climb. If you do not help me, I shall collapse upon these stones."

The haughty horse tossed his flowing mane and snorted in contempt: "Do you take me for a common beast of burden? Toil is your station in life, while mine is to look regal. Walk on, and do not whine!"

A mile further on, the exhausted donkey gave a deep, shuddering groan, collapsed onto the flint stones, and died of sheer exhaustion.

The peddler wept for his lost donkey, but had no time to lose. He unbuckled all the heavy baggage, pots, and sacks of grain, and hoisted every single ounce onto the back of the proud horse. And to crown the load, he flayed the donkey and threw the heavy skin on top!

Staggering beneath the crushing weight, his back groaning under the double burden, the horse groaned in bitter remorse: "Alas, what a fool I was! By refusing to help my brother with a small sack, I am now forced to carry his entire load and his skin into the bargain!"
moral: Refusing to share a brother’s small burden often forces you to bear the entire load alone.
